content.text:
I submitted index 0 (Al₀.₉₀Sb₀.₁₀) as the best composition, but its EQE (external quantum efficiency) was only 0.0019%. All three compositions I measured are effectively at zero, so no composition on this line clearly works as a photoanode.

- **Why so little signal:** Al and Sb oxides only absorb light with more energy than 2.1 eV. The 2.1 eV illumination in this setup is below that, so near-zero response was expected everywhere on the line.
- **What I measured:** with only 3 measurements available, I spread them across the line:

| Index | Composition | EQE (%) |
|---|---|---|
| 0 | Al₀.₉₀Sb₀.₁₀ (Al-rich end) | 0.0019 |
| 10 | Al₀.₅₁Sb₀.₄₉ (midpoint) | −0.0012 |
| 20 | Al₀.₁₁Sb₀.₈₉ (Sb-rich end) | 0.0006 |

- **How reliable the pick is:** the differences between these values are about the size of the measurement noise. Index 0 won on the numbers, not because it's clearly a better material.
- **What I didn't use:** none of the 5 XRD measurements. Knowing the crystal structures wouldn't have helped choose between compositions with no measurable response.
